script: [serious] In 1977, a radio telescope in Ohio heard something from space. And it never heard it again. August 15th. Ohio State's Big Ear telescope picked up a narrow, powerful signal that lasted seventy-two seconds, close to the frequency of hydrogen, the exact kind of signal astronomers thought an alien civilization might use. Days later, astronomer Jerry Ehman saw it on a printout, circled the code six E Q U J five, and wrote one word in red ink. Wow. Telescopes have pointed at that patch of sky again and again. Nothing. In 2024, researchers proposed a natural cause, a cloud of hydrogen suddenly brightened by a powerful burst from a dead star. But no one has proven it. Aliens, or the universe playing a trick? You decide. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number twenty-three. A new file every day.
